item.title: Why I ditched Atiku – Okowa
item.description: Former Delta State Governor and 2023 running mate to Atiku Abubakar, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, has explained why he is now supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Speaking on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Okowa said he had “seen the light.” “I have seen the light. Today, we are on the right track because the president is laying a solid foundation,” he declared. Okowa warned against any return of the fuel subsidy, stating that those who previously destroyed Nigeria’s foundation through the subsidy regime must not be allowed to “destroy the future of our children.” At the same rally, Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, set a target of 2.3 million votes for Tinubu in Rivers State in the January 16 election. He said the figure was achievable, noting that about 2.8 million Permanent Voter Cards had been collected out of 3.3 million registered voters in the state. Yari asked supporters to back Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike in delivering the votes and described Rivers as a state from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent.” Senate President Godswill Akpabio noted that Rivers was the only South-South state Tinubu won convincingly in 2023 and expressed confidence that the feat would be repeated. He also claimed that under Tinubu, Nigeria now generates more revenue from taxation than from crude oil. APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria,” while Senator Magnus Abe defended the Rainbow Coalition in the state, saying its main interest was to return the president to power. item.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
item.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. item.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future. Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation. “To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said. Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said. The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared. He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations. “The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said. He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments. “A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added. item.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
item.description: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team. In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000. AFA also stated it would now take its appeals against its own and Paredes’s sanctions to CAS. The post Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Re-election: Tinubu lists economy, education, healthcare as priorities
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to give priority attention to education, economic recovery, healthcare and citizens’ welfare if given another mandate in 2027. Tinubu made the pledge at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt on Saturday. Speaking at the rally co-organised by the Rainbow Coalition led by Chief Nyesom Wike, the Minister, Federal Capital Territory, Tinubu also said that youth development would be given deserved attention. The president urged Rivers people to use their Permanent Voter Cards wisely to achieve a better and more progressive Nigeria. He expressed his administration’s commitment to promote the welfare of retirees through enhanced and prompt payment of pensions and gratuities. He commended Wike and the people of Rivers for massively expressing their resolve to support his re-election bid. The president thanked Wike for his commitment to reconciliation and peace-building during the political crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu also commended Gov. Siminalayi Fubara for being a peaceful leader and lover of his state, saying, “The governor will never regret his commitment to restoring peace in the state.” “I sincerely appreciate Wike, Fubara, APC members and the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council for their support,” he said. Earlier, Wike assured the president that Rivers residents would massively support his re-election bid. He said that Tinubu had demonstrated huge support to the state by appointing no fewer than 47 Rivers people into strategic positions at the national level. “We cannot take the president’s support for granted. Rivers people will vote massively for the president in the 2027 presidential election,” he said. Also speaking, Fubara said that Rivers would deliver no fewer than three million votes in support of the president’s re-election bid. “We shall continue to work together to ensure that the president wins the election; that is our promise,” he said. He thanked the campaign team for providing an opportunity for Rivers people to demonstrate their political strength and support for the president. Fubara thanked Tinubu for his commitment to the development of the Niger Delta Region through critical infrastructure projects, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that while in the state, Tinubu inaugurated the Bonny-Bodo Road project. He also presented the APC governorship flag to the party’s candidate in Rivers, Mr Kingsley Chinda. item.title: Hope you’ll visit 33 other states after Akwa Ibom ‘sleep’ – Obi tells Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to extend his visits to the remaining 33 states of the federation after spending a night in Akwa Ibom State. bi made the call in a post on X on Saturday, following Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where the president said his overnight stay would be a “second term presidential sleep” ahead of the 2027 election. Obi congratulated Tinubu on spending a night in a state outside Lagos and Abuja, urging the president to use such visits to engage directly with Nigerians and explain the impact of his administration. He said he hoped the Akwa Ibom visit would encourage Tinubu to travel to the other 33 states, spend time with the people and account for the resources accruing to the Federal Government. “I sincerely hope this visit will inspire you to travel to the remaining 33 states of the federation, spend time with the people and, more importantly, explain what your administration has done with the ₦15.8 trillion saved from the removal of fuel subsidy, the over $100 billion you have borrowed, the increased revenues accruing to the government from taxing Nigerians, and the additional government revenues which your administration celebrated last year as having surpassed its target,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor also demanded explanations on the impact of government policies on poverty, education, healthcare and electricity. He asked the President to state how many Nigerians had been lifted out of poverty, how many out-of-school children had returned to school and how many functional primary healthcare centres had been built. Obi also questioned the improvement in electricity supply, recalling Tinubu’s earlier promise that Nigerians should not vote for him if his administration failed to fix the power sector. On insecurity, he said Nigerians deserved an explanation of what the government had done to secure the country, which he noted still ranks among the world’s most terrorised countries. “Mr President, Nigerians deserve answers. They deserve to know what has been done with the resources entrusted to your government,” Obi said. He added that the New Nigeria he seeks to build would be founded on accountability, transparency and the measurable impact of public resources on citizens. Tinubu had on Friday told supporters at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom, describing it as a “second term presidential sleep” and expressing confidence in securing re-election in 2027. item.title: PVC Is Your Weapon Against Poverty, Tinubu Tells Supporters In Rivers
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Saturday urged supporters in Rivers State to use their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to vote for what he described as the progressive development of the Nigerian economy, saying it was their weapon against poverty. Tinubu made the appeal while addressing supporters at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, the Rivers State capital, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally ahead of the 2027 general elections. The President urged those who had yet to collect their PVCs to do so, stressing that the card was the instrument available to them to fight poverty through the ballot. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have, and that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please, I beg you, I take God beg. The weapon you have against poverty is to elect progressive development of our economy. That is what I am pursuing,” Tinubu said. ﻿ Addressing Nigerian youths, the President said the outcome of the 2027 elections would have a direct impact on their future, urging them to take the exercise seriously. “To the youths of Nigeria, I am looking at you. This election is about you, it’s not on me. Your future depends on this election. This progress has no reverse gear,” he said. The Rivers campaign comes a day after Tinubu attended an APC rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where Governor Umo Eno pledged two million votes for the President in the 2027 election. At the rally, Tinubu also approved Eno’s request for the establishment of the Ibom Deep Sea Port, describing the project as a catalyst for development in the state and the South-South region. The Rivers rally attracted APC leaders and supporters from across the state and the South-South geopolitical zone. Those who also addressed the gathering and canvassed support for the party included Vice President Kashim Shettima, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara and Senate President Godswill Akpabio, among other party leaders. item.title: Ebola: DRC records 10,668 cases, 5,198 deaths — WHO
item.description: The disease, Bundibugyo virus disease, with transmission continuing across eight provinces, the World Health Organization (WHO) says. The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that the figure recorded was as of Nov. 3, representing a case fatality ratio of 48.7 percent. It said the outbreak had spread geographically, with active transmission ongoing in 51 of the 67 affected health zones across eight provinces. According to WHO, although some areas have recorded a slight decline in cases, sustained and high-level transmission continues across DRC. The organization said 512 deaths had been reported since Oct. 21, comprising 335 deaths in communities and 177 in treatment centers. It expressed concern over the high number of community deaths, particularly among young children, attributing the trend to challenges in early detection and timely access to appropriate healthcare. “No new cases had been reported in Kenya and Nigeria since its previous Disease Outbreak News published on Oct. 23. “However, there is the need for sustained regional preparedness, including cross-border surveillance, monitoring at points of entry, early case detection, and coordinated response measures,” it said. The organization also disclosed that Switzerland and the United Kingdom had medically evacuated confirmed cases involving their citizens, although no new country had reported cases since the previous update. WHO advised against imposing travel or trade restrictions on countries experiencing or responding to the outbreak, based on currently available information. item.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
item.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

item.title: Tinubu-Shettima ticket most formidable in Nigeria’s history, says APC chair
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the most formidable in Nigeria’s political history, urging Nigerians to support their re-election in 2027. Yilwatda said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the economic reforms and infrastructure projects initiated by his administration. He made the remarks on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition Presidential Campaign Rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said the Tinubu-Shettima ticket combined political experience, courage and leadership capacity needed to address the country’s challenges. “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country. He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria,” he said. Yilwatda defended the administration’s economic policies, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing them as necessary steps towards rebuilding the economy and strengthening public finances. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had created difficulties for households and businesses, he said the government was working to cushion their effects through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions and infrastructure investments. The APC chairman also praised Tinubu’s infrastructure programme, particularly major highway projects, which he said would improve connectivity, facilitate trade and create economic opportunities. “We have a President who understands that development cannot happen without infrastructure. He has initiated an ambitious infrastructure revolution through major highway projects that will connect different parts of Nigeria, open up economic corridors, facilitate the movement of goods and services and create new opportunities for our people,” Yilwatda said. He urged Nigerians to support the continuation of the administration’s policies, arguing that a second term would allow Tinubu to consolidate the reforms and deliver their expected benefits. Turning to Rivers State, Yilwatda commended political leaders and members of the Rainbow Coalition for supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid across party lines. He said the growing political cooperation in the state reflected a shared commitment to national development, irrespective of party affiliation. “Come 2027, we want to continue with this reformer and performer as our President. item.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. item.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
item.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. item.title: 2027: Collect campaign money, but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect money offered to them by politicians during campaigns but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice during his presidential campaign flag-off in Bauchi, where he addressed supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged voters not to allow financial inducements to influence their electoral choices, insisting that accepting money from politicians should not translate into voting against their conscience. “When they bring money, it’s your money. Collect it, spend it, but vote your heart, and I know your heart is with us and with APM,” he told the gathering. The APM presidential candidate also called on Nigerians to support what he described as a national reset, arguing that economic hardship, insecurity and lack of inclusiveness in governance had made fundamental changes necessary. He questioned whether hunger among Nigerians should not prompt an economic reset, just as insecurity required a review of the country’s security architecture. Makinde further argued that the exclusion of many Nigerians from governance demanded a reset of the country’s socio-political environment. He said Nigerians dissatisfied with the state of affairs should embrace the proposed national reset, adding that the country needed a government capable of addressing public concerns with sincerity and transparency. He also appreciated Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, whom he described as his national leader, the APM national chairman, and his wife for their support and encouragement. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s developments centre on President Tinubu’s new infrastructure commitment during his South-South campaign, fresh World Bank figures on Nigeria’s external debt, and the release of long-stranded electricity equipment. In Africa, Sudan’s humanitarian agencies warn of a serious funding shortfall. Globally, AI-related stocks have recovered some of Thursday’s losses, although investors remain concerned about technology spending and regulation. 1. Nigeria 2027: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport project during South-South campaign ﻿ What happened: President Bola Tinubu announced approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Seaport at an APC rally in Uyo on Friday, 6 November, in response to a request from Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno. Eno described the project as critical to the state’s maritime economy and pledged to mobilise two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. That is a political commitment, not an electoral forecast. The president is scheduled to attend another APC rally in Port Harcourt today. Why it matters: The long-delayed seaport could expand Nigeria’s cargo-handling capacity and support manufacturing, logistics and international trade if successfully financed and constructed. Strategic implications: The announcement links an important economic infrastructure proposal with the ongoing election campaign. Presidential approval does not yet establish an agreed financing structure or construction timetable. What to watch: Formal project approval documents, funding arrangements, implementation milestones and today’s Rivers State campaign activities. 2. Nigeria economy: World Bank puts total external debt at $145 billion The World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC, on April 13, 2022. The Spring meetings will take place virtually from April 22-25. Stefani Reynolds / AFP What happened: The World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, released on 5 November and reported extensively on Friday, shows that Nigeria’s total external debt rose by 6.6% to $145.02 billion at the end of 2025. Nigerian Debt 2024 external debt $135.99bn 2025 external debt $145.02bn Public/guaranteed 43% Private 38% Short-term 19% The total includes approximately $62.4 billion in public and publicly guaranteed obligations, $54.5 billion in private nonguaranteed debt and $28.1 billion in short-term obligations. It must not be confused with government external debt alone. Why it matters: External debt servicing is consuming more export earnings, even as some indicators of debt sustainability have improved. Business and political implications: The figures warrant careful scrutiny alongside Tinubu’s revised $7.7 billion external borrowing proposal. Borrowing costs, project productivity and fiscal transparency will remain central to the government’s economic policy debate. What to watch: Legislative scrutiny of new borrowing, financing terms, debt-service projections and independently measured returns on infrastructure spending. 3. item.title: AFCON 2027 Race: Chelle names Ndidi, Simon, Iwobi, Bassey, 21 others for Tanzania
item.description: Head Coach Éric Chelle has selected team captain Wilfred Ndidi, defenders Calvin Bassey and Semi Ajayi, midfielders Alex Iwobi and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, and forwards Moses Simon, Ademola Lookman and Akor Adams in his 24-man roster for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars this month. On the list as well are goalkeepers Stanley Nwabali and Arthur Okonkwo, defendes Olaoluwa Aina and Benjamin Fredricks, midfielders Tochukwu Nnadi and Samson Tijani, and forwards Moses Usor and Taiwo Awoniyi. Turkey-based defender Chibuike Nwaiwu and Czechia-based wing-back Abdullahi Bewene are also called. The Super Eagles host tournament joint-hosts Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Friday, 13th November, before flying out for the return against the Taifa Stars at Zanzibar’s Amman Stadium on Tuesday, 17th November. Nigeria, currently in second position in Group L, must win both games to improve their chances of picking the only ticket from the pool for the final tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda next summer. item.title: Rivers chose Tinubu, says Wike
item.description: Nyesom Wike, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, said the people of Rivers State have chosen President Bola Tinubu as their candidate in the January 2027 presidential election. Read Also: You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu Wike said this on Saturday while welcoming Tinubu and his delegation to the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt for the president’s campaign rally. He is the coordinator of the presidential campaign council in the state. Wike said: “Your Excellency, this is Rivers State’s rally. We did not mobilise anybody from any other state. You can see with your eyes that the people of Rivers State have already concluded and agreed that on January 16, they will vote for you. “Since the inception of democracy in 1999, Rivers people have never had it this way. We have no less than 47 political appointments from Mr President. “So, who is our brother? Our brother is Bola Ahmed Tinubu because he has identified with the people of Rivers state. He described President Tinubu as a political ally of Rivers people, saying the president had demonstrated his commitment to the state through federal projects and political appointments. Also, Wike took a swipe at Rotimi Amaechi’s projects. He questioned the outcome of an alleged fumigation exercise in Rivers, saying it had failed to eliminate mosquitoes. “All we are saying to the vice-presidential candidate is, please, come and give an account of how you fumigated Rivers state. You fumigated Rivers state so that there would be no mosquitoes. “Have mosquitoes gone? Are mosquitoes not biting you?” He recalled Amaechi’s role as director-general of the presidential campaigns of former President Muhammadu Buhari. Wike said the then APC candidate failed to secure up to 15 percent of the votes in Rivers state in the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections. item.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. item.title: Makinde: Tinubu’s poor planning plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed the economic hardship facing millions of Nigerians on what he described as inadequate planning by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. Makinde said major economic policy decisions introduced by the Federal Government were implemented without adequate plans and frameworks to cushion their effects on citizens, thereby worsening the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians. The APM presidential candidate spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), while in Bauchi State to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign. He argued that the immediate impact of the administration’s economic policies on Nigerians was a consequence of taking major decisions without adequate preparation and effective implementation strategies. Makinde stressed that economic reforms must be supported by proper planning and clear implementation frameworks to ensure that ordinary citizens do not bear the brunt of government policies. He said addressing the country’s economic challenges would require fundamental structural reforms and strong political will. The Oyo governor also highlighted the APM’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, which he said was designed to address the country’s challenges through a documented policy framework and the party’s manifesto. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that recognises and respects Nigeria’s diverse nationalities.
